data.narrative:
Mainspring Energy is a Series F climate and energy technology company that has raised $650M+ to date. The valuation exercise draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies in the Climate & Energy sector: one public entity (LNZA) and eight private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables at similar valuation tiers to support a robust peer-median approach, limiting triangulation to stage-progression methodology alone.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.3x step-up multiplier to the $650M total raised proxy, a typical valuation advancement for Series F progression to later institutional funding rounds. This method yields an implied valuation of $845M. Given the absence of reliable peer multiples, the single-method framework produces a range anchored at the median: a low bound of $718M (approximately 15% below median) and a high bound of $972M (approximately 15% above median), reflecting estimation bands around the stage-progression point estimate rather than truly independent methodological convergence.

The $845M median valuation represents a defensible Series F reference point given available inputs, but the analysis rests on limited triangulation. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage comparable transactions and the early-stage nature of the Climate & Energy sector's public comparables, which may not reflect private frontier-tech risk dynamics. A broader peer dataset or recent transaction data in deep tech energy would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
